editorial.thesis: A office-led-and-learning city of about 1.9 million. Its retail is heavy on pharmacy & health retail and fitness & wellness, and thin on desserts, sweets & ice cream and apparel, footwear & jewellery — and 22% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 60% of Delhi's. 11.28 chain outlets per lakh residents against 18.83 in Delhi; 37 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Domino's 36, Bata 20, Apollo Pharmacy 16.

The mapped economy leans to offices. Shares of all mapped places: offices 17.2% (Delhi 11.7%); education 11.5% (Delhi 7.9%); desserts & sweets 0.4% (Delhi 0.7%); grocery & daily needs 1.4% (Delhi 2.2%). Raw counts would mislead because Delhi is mapped more completely (87,703 places against 14,695), so we compare mix, not counts.

Supply and demand are misaligned. 1 zones hold 22% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Chawla Colony · Tigaon Road alone has about 391,000 residents and 59 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is less concentrated than in Delhi. 44% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Delhi 47%). The largest cores are Neelam Bata Road · Sainik Colony (2,530 places) and Huda Market · Main Market (1,409).

The widest brand gaps against Delhi. Café Coffee Day 6 outlets vs 145; Domino's 36 outlets vs 140; Apollo Pharmacy 16 outlets vs 108. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 10 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Delhi, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Chawla Colony · Tigaon Road and Neelam Bata Road · Sainik Colony are the largest zones by residents (391,000 and 332,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 44% of all commercial places, and Neelam Bata Road · Sainik Colony alone lists 2,530.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Neelam Bata Road · Sainik Colony holds 51 of the 214 tracked chain outlets, and Mathura Road · Huda Market adds 42.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Neelam Bata Road · Sainik Colony and Huda Market · Main Market lead on education places (291 and 211, with 100 and 77 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Chawla Colony · Tigaon Road. The blue cores include Neelam Bata Road · Sainik Colony.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (87,703 places in Delhi against 14,695 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Delhi; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Delhi, Faridabad's mapped places over-index on offices (17.2% vs 11.7%), education (11.5% vs 7.9%), healthcare (9.8% vs 6.9%) and under-index on desserts & sweets (0.4% vs 0.7%), grocery & daily needs (1.4% vs 2.2%), hotels & stays (3.0% vs 4.4%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 214 outlets of 37 tracked national brands within 10 km — 11.28 per lakh residents against Delhi's 18.83 (1289 outlets of 45 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Delhi are Café Coffee Day (6 vs 145); Domino's (36 vs 140); Apollo Pharmacy (16 vs 108). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Delhi's, so low means thin by Delhi's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 10 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Faridabad's age mix against Delhi: children (0–14) 27.6% vs 23.1%, 15–24 20.4% vs 20.4%, working age 45.7% vs 49.7%, 60+ 6.3% vs 6.8%. Under-25s are 48% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 4.4% of mapped places against 5.7% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 36 (Delhi 140), Pizza Hut 11 (Delhi 68), Subway 10 (Delhi 55), McDonald's 8 (Delhi 75).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 1.6% of mapped places against 2.1% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 6 (Delhi 145), Chaayos 3 (Delhi 18), Blue Tokai 3 (Delhi 26), Starbucks 2 (Delhi 33). No mapped outlet in either city: Chai Sutta Bar.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.4% of mapped places against 0.7% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 4 (Delhi 29), Theobroma 1 (Delhi 11). No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.4% of mapped places against 2.2% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 6 (Delhi 21), More 5 (Delhi 2), Big Bazaar 2 (Delhi 8), Spencer's 2 (Delhi 9). No mapped outlet in either city: Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.5% of mapped places against 1.2% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 16 (Delhi 108). No mapped outlet in either city: MedPlus, Wellness Forever, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 4.0% of mapped places against 7.0% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 20 (Delhi 66), Raymond 9 (Delhi 55), Tanishq 7 (Delhi 20), Westside 4 (Delhi 15).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 8.3% of mapped places against 7.9% in Delhi, so the mix is level.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 3.1% of mapped places against 2.7% in Delhi — above its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 4.4% of mapped places against 3.9% in Delhi — above its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
